newsitem.title: USA: US junk bond funds get $296 mln in new cash-AMG.
newsitem.headline: US junk bond funds get $296 mln in new cash-AMG.

text.p: U.S. high-yield bond mutual funds received net cash inflows of $296 million in the latest recorded week which ended July 23, according to AMG Data Services.
Including this week's number, U.S. junk bond mutual funds have received positive net cash inflows for each of the past eight consecutive weeks.
In the prior two weeks, inflows totalled $310.4 million and $389 million, respectively, AMG reported.
The information is tallied from high-yield bond funds that report on a weekly basis only. AMG excludes reinvested distributions, therefore representing only net new money coming into funds.
Mutual fund cash flows are closely watched by junk bond players because the high-yield bond market has one of the heaviest concentrations of mutual fund money of any major asset class in the U.S.
Analysts estimate 25-40 percent of all outstanding junk bonds are held by mutual funds.
AMG, based in Arcata, Calif. compiles information on U.S. mutual funds.
